decisions.reason: Real breach with concrete scope: logistics partner ShipMonk compromised, attackers accessed order data (full names, shipping addresses, emails, phone numbers) for nearly 14,000 Trezor customers in the US, UK, Sweden, Colombia, Brazil, Italy, and Portugal with orders between May 10 and August 8, 2026. No CVEs involved.

Korean-language roundup of the same August 2026 Patch Tuesday wave: Windows 10 cumulative update KB5120249 and Windows 11 KB5121003, 400 total vulns including 2 zero-days, 176 privilege-escalation, 11 security-feature bypass, 110 remote-code-execution. Belongs in the tracked Patch Tuesday story, not a separate one.
AlphaHunt deep-research essay on malicious dependencies and AI-assisted code review workflows. Analysis piece with no concrete incident, no CVE, no victim or campaign detail.
Cybersecurity M&A deals roundup for July 2026. Business news, not a security event, vulnerability, or breach.

SecurityWeek report on the same Adobe Commerce/Magento flaw already tracked (CVE-2026-71362, incorrect authorization, CVSS 9.1) being targeted immediately after disclosure, matching the Sansec WAF-blocked exploitation wave in the existing story. Same incident, additional outlet.

Insikt Group research profiling 24 threat actors advertising crypting services over the past year: payload wrapping, in-memory execution, anti-analysis, process injection, persistence, and post-detection re-crypting, with a Windows-payload focus. Substantive threat-actor-economy research; same article as the Recorded Future piece (mf:160103).

Canadian Centre for Cyber Security advisory AV26-814 (2026-08-13): GitLab before 19.0.6, 19.1.4, and 19.2.2 affected; patch releases named. Advisory with substance though it names no CVE IDs and makes no exploitation claim.
Vendor thought-leadership byline (ActiveState Head of Product) on the scale challenge of vetting open source for AI ingestion. Marketing-adjacent explainer, no incident or vulnerability.

BleepingComputer coverage of the same White House memo already tracked: NCC program letting private security firms apply for approval to conduct offensive cyber operations (hack-back) against foreign cyber-enabled transnational criminal organizations. Same story as the existing cyberscoop/other coverage.

Original Recorded Future Insikt Group analysis of the crypting-services market (24 advertising actors, reputation-driven, Windows payloads); identical substance to the malware.news syndication mf:160109. One story.
